method: Each claim checked against retrieved text of the RACGP handbook pages. Statements the source marks consensus-based are labelled as such. Points not isolated in the retrieved text are listed unresolved, not asserted.

claims.claim: A reasonable HbA1c goal for many non-pregnant adults is <7% (53 mmol/mol) without significant hypoglycaemia
claims.source_text: A reasonable HbA1c goal for many non-pregnant adults is <7% (53 mmol/mol) without significant hypoglycaemia is appropriate.

claims.claim: Older people: target may be 8% (64 mmol/mol) rather than 7% (53 mmol/mol)
claims.source_text: Glycaemic targets for some elderly people may be higher than for the non-elderly (eg an HbA1c target of 8% [64 mmol/mol] rather than 7% [53 mmol/mol]).

claims.claim: SMBG targets 4.0-7.0 mmol/L fasting and preprandial, 5.0-10.0 mmol/L two-hour postprandial
claims.source_text: Targets for SMBG levels are 4.0-7.0 mmol/L for fasting and preprandial, and 5.0-10.0 mmol/L for two-hour postprandial.

claims.claim: CGM/Flash target 3.9-10 mmol/L
claims.source_text: Recommended glycaemic targets for users of CGM/FlashGM with type 2 diabetes: a target of 3.9-10 mmol/L

claims.claim: Dose adjustments and/or additions to attain target HbA1c within 3-6 months
claims.source_text: Dose adjustments to, and/or addition of, glucose-lowering medications should be made in order to attain target glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) within 3-6 months.

claims.claim: Remission defined as HbA1c below 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) for at least three months without glucose-lowering medications; consensus-based
claims.source_text: Intensive lifestyle changes, including weight loss, may achieve diabetes remission (defined as glycated haemoglobin [HbA1c] levels remaining below 6.5% [48 mmol/mol] for at least three months in the absence of glucose-lowering medications). *Consensus-based recommendation

claims.claim: Metabolic surgery for selected non-pregnant adults BMI 27-45, duration <6 years, HbA1c <12%, not using insulin
claims.source_text: induce type 2 diabetes remission to selected non-pregnant adults with a body mass index (BMI) between 27 and 45 kg/m2, type 2 diabetes duration <6 years, HbA1c <12% and not using insulin

claims.claim: Metabolic surgery also considered at BMI 30.0-34.9 if hyperglycaemia inadequately managed despite optimal oral or injectable treatment; consensus-based
claims.source_text: Metabolic surgery should also be considered for people with type 2 diabetes and BMI 30.0-34.9 kg/m2 if hyperglycaemia is inadequately managed despite optimal treatment with either oral or in[jectable]

claims.claim: Add SGLT2i in adults with type 2 diabetes who also have CVD, multiple cardiovascular risk factors and/or kidney disease
claims.source_text: We recommend the addition of an sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) to other glucose-lowering medication(s) in adults with type 2 diabetes who also have CVD, multiple cardiovascular risk factors* and/or kidney disease

claims.claim: Add GLP-1RA where unable to be prescribed an SGLT2i due to intolerance or contraindication
claims.source_text: agonist (GLP-1RA) to other glucose-lowering medication(s) in adults with type 2 diabetes who have CVD, multiple cardiovascular risk factors* and/or kidney disease, and are unable to be prescribed an SGLT2i due to either intoleranc[e or contraindication]

claims.claim: SGLT2i separately recommended in adults with type 2 diabetes who also have kidney disease
claims.source_text: We recommend the addition of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) to other glucose-lowering medication(s) in adults with type 2 diabetes who also have kidney disease.

claims.claim: If glycaemic targets are not achieved, other classes should be added or substituted; consensus-based
claims.source_text: If glycaemic targets are not achieved, other classes of glucose-lowering agents should be added or substituted to improve glycaemic control** ... Consensus

claims.claim: Obesity pharmacotherapy considered alongside lifestyle change
claims.source_text: Obesity pharmacotherapy should be considered for people with diabetes and overweight or obesity along with lifestyle changes.

claims.claim: Any effective first-line antihypertensive recommended; ACEi or ARB first-line in diabetes with coronary artery disease
claims.source_text: In patients with diabetes and hypertension, any of the first-line* antihypertensive drugs that effectively lower blood pressure are recommended. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi) or (ARBs) angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are recommended first-line therapy for hypertension in people with diabetes and coronary artery disease.

claims.claim: Examine higher-risk patients without retinopathy at least annually; annual screening for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people; consensus-based
claims.source_text: Examine higher-risk patients who do not have diabetic retinopathy (DR) at least annually (high risk defined as: longer duration of diabetes; suboptimal glycaemic management, blood pressure o[r ...]) ... Conduct annual DR screening for Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander people with diabetes.

claims.claim: Low-risk feet: annual foot examination; consensus-based
claims.source_text: In people stratified as having low-risk feet (where no risk factors or previous foot complications have been identified), foot examination should occur annually.

claims.claim: People aged 18-30 with early-onset type 2 diabetes: consider timely endocrinologist referral; consensus-based
claims.source_text: For people aged 18-30 years with early-onset type 2 diabetes, due to the complexity of management and higher risk of complications, consider timely referral to an endocrinologist

claims.claim: Sick-day management plans integral to diabetes education
claims.source_text: Sick-day management plans are an integral component of diabetes education. The development of a sick-day management plan along with education on sick-day management should be

claims.claim: Inform people on SGLT2i about DKA risk associated with clinical procedures, ideally with written information and management plans
claims.source_text: SGLT2i), clinicians should inform them about the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) associated with clinical procedures, ideally with written information and management plans

claims.claim: ns-MRA an option where eGFR >=25 mL/min/1.73m2
claims.source_text: a GLP-1 agonist or a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (if eGFR is >=25 mL/min/1.73 m2)

claims.claim: PBS: metformin restricted; sulfonylureas and insulin glargine unrestricted; SGLT2i, GLP-1RA, DPP-4i, finerenone authority; ertugliflozin, exenatide, liraglutide, tirzepatide not listed
claims.source_text: Schedule 4333 items query: Metformin 96 ['R']; Gliclazide 24 ['R','U']; Glimepiride 22 ['R','U']; Empagliflozin 22 ['S']; Dapagliflozin 16 ['S']; Semaglutide 6 ['A','S']; Dulaglutide 2 ['A','S']; Sitagliptin 100 ['S']; Linagliptin 8 ['S']; Pioglitazone 18 ['R']; Finerenone 2 ['S']; Insulin glargine 4 ['U']; Ertugliflozin, Exenatide, Liraglutide, Tirzepatide no rows

claims.claim: Metformin is first-line
claims.note: The medical-management page discusses metformin throughout but an explicit first-line statement was not isolated in the retrieved text. Listed unresolved rather than asserted from background knowledge.
